evals.name: returns-portal-brd-mvp-stories
evals.prompt: Returns portal BRD (summary): Customers of an online furniture store can start a return within 30 days of delivery from their order page, pick items and a reason, choose pickup or drop-off, and get a prepaid label by email. Items over 40 kg need scheduled pickup. Refunds go to the original payment method within 5 business days of the warehouse scan. Customer service agents can override the 30-day window with a reason code. Warehouse staff scan returned items and mark condition (resellable, damaged, missing parts). Damaged-on-arrival claims need a photo upload. Turn this into epics and user stories with acceptance criteria, MVP scope only, and write them to stories.md. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
evals.expected_output: The skill sets MVP at 10-15 stories, epics with a 5-10 word title, 2-4 sentence description and 3-5 key objectives, specific personas instead of 'user/admin', 3-8 testable criteria per story that include error and edge cases, and no implementation detail; an unguided answer often over-produces stories, uses generic personas, or covers only the happy path.
expectations: MVP scope: 10-15 stories in As a / I want / so that form

Epic structure per the skill: title, 2-4 sentence business objective, 3-5 key objectives, list of stories; stories have a 3-8 word title, As a/I want/so that, and 3-8 criteria: Every epic and story follows the structure

Edge and error cases from the BRD are in criteria: return attempted after 30 days, >40 kg forces scheduled pickup, damaged claim blocked without photo, agent override requires a reason code, refund timing from warehouse scan: All five covered

Personas are specific (customer, customer service agent, warehouse associate), stories are independent and sprint-sized, and the BRD is fully traced (no requirement dropped, label email and condition marking included): Specific personas, independent stories, full coverage

Criteria describe observable behavior, not implementation (no databases, queues, frameworks, endpoints) and no invented business rules beyond the source; assumptions are listed: No implementation detail and assumptions labeled
Does not ask the user questions; lists the assumptions it made in stories.md and in its final message.

scripted_checks.text: MVP scope: 10-15 stories in As a / I want / so that form
scripted_checks.check: python3 -c 'import re,sys;n=len(re.findall(r"As an? [^,\n]+?,? I want .+? so that",open("stories.md").read(),re.I|re.S));sys.exit(0 if 10<=n<=15 else 1)'

evals.name: acceptance-criteria-six-stories-sso-conflict
evals.prompt: Write acceptance criteria for these existing stories and save them to ac.md: (1) As a tenant admin, I want to invite teammates by email so that they can join our workspace. (2) As a tenant admin, I want to remove a teammate so that former staff lose access. (3) As a compliance officer, I want to export the audit log for a date range so that I can answer auditors. (4) As a teammate, I want to reset my password so that I can get back in. (5) As a tenant admin, I want to require SSO so that nobody signs in with a password. (6) As a compliance officer, I want audit entries kept for 7 years so that we meet retention rules. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
evals.expected_output: The skill's gate treats missing error conditions and vague terms as failures and wants 3-8 observable criteria per story; it should also notice story 4 conflicts with story 5 once SSO is required. An unguided answer tends to list happy-path checks and miss lockout and last-admin cases.
expectations: Error and edge conditions: expired or reused invite, inviting an existing member, removing the last admin, removed user sessions/tokens revoked, invalid or too-large date range, SSO enforcement locking out admins without a recovery path, deleting or editing entries before 7 years: At least five of these
Notices the conflict between story 4 (password reset) and story 5 (require SSO) and states the expected behavior when SSO is enforced: Conflict identified with a concrete criterion
Each story has 3-8 criteria, phrased as observable outcomes with measurable terms (time limits, counts, explicit messages): All six stories in range and measurable

Criteria describe observable behavior, not implementation (no databases, queues, frameworks, endpoints) and no invented business rules beyond the source; assumptions are listed: No implementation detail and assumptions labeled
Every one of the six stories has between 3 and 8 acceptance criteria.

scripted_checks.check: python3 -c 'import re,sys;t=open("ac.md").read();P=["invite", "remove", "export", "reset", "SSO", "7 years|seven years|retention"];sys.exit(0 if sum(bool(re.search(p,t,re.I)) for p in P)>=6 else 1)'
